lessons.title: Question: Different comparisons
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which operators can we use to make comparisons for if statement conditions?

>=, <=, > and <= and &&None of them

>=, <=, > and <.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which set can compare one numeric value with another in an if condition?

>=, <=, >, and <= and &&let and const

>=, <=, >, and <.

lessons.title: Example: Good decisions
lessons.interactiveContent:
Write a comparison that displays the text if flightPrice is less than or equal to budget.

Make sure to pick flightPrice, followed by <=, and finally budget.
lessons.hardModeContent:
With flightPrice on the left, check that it does not exceed budget to display Book your flight!.

Make sure to pick flightPrice, followed by <=, and finally budget.

lessons.title: Question: Condition
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we compare two numbers of different values with ===?

We get the boolean trueWe get the boolean falseWe get a number

We get the boolean false.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Evaluate 4 === 7. What value does this comparison produce?

The boolean falseThe boolean trueThe number 3

Make sure to pick The boolean false.

lessons.title: Question: Variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why should we sometimes store the results of comparisons in variables?

To reuse the results of the comparisonsTo always skip a block of codeTo always run a block of code

To reuse the results of the comparisons.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You store score > 10 in a variable before an if statement. Why store that comparison result?

So the same true-or-false result can be reused.So the if block always runs.So score is automatically changed to 10.

So the same true-or-false result can be reused.

lessons.title: Example: Variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use a variable that stores the result of a comparison as the if statement's condition.

Make sure to pick multiPlayer.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the stored multiplayer result to print the setup message when more than one player joins.

Make sure to pick >, followed by 1, and finally multiPlayer.

lessons.title: Question: Else
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we call the part of an if / else statement that runs when the if statement's condition is false?

An else statementThere is no such conditionalAn if statement

An else statement.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An if condition is false. Which keyword introduces the alternative block that can run?

elseelseifthen

Make sure to pick else.

lessons.title: Example: Else
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an empty if statement (has no code block) that checks if membership equals "gold", followed by an empty else statement.

Make sure to pick if followed by (membership === "gold") and then }, else, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Write empty if and else blocks that test whether membership is gold.

Make sure to pick 'gold', followed by if, membership, ===, and finally else.

lessons.title: Question: No own condition
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why doesn't the else statement have its own condition between parentheses?

Because its code block will always run if the if condition is not metBecause it always runs so it doesn't need a conditionThe else statement does have a condition between parentheses

Because its code block will always run if the if condition is not met.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You change an if condition from false to true. What happens to its else block?

It stops running because the if condition is now met.It still runs because else always runs.It runs after the if block to check the same condition again.

It stops running because the if condition is now met.

lessons.title: Question: Catch all
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when commonFriends has a value smaller than 3?

The else statement's code block runsThe if statement's code block runsNeither the if code block nor the else statement's code block run

The else statement's code block runs.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Imagine commonFriends has the value 2 before this conditional runs. Which branch would that value select?

No new suggestionsFriend suggestions: SueIt prints the number 2.

Make sure to pick No new suggestions.
